Weigh the whole pot after cooking, minus the pot. Cooking changes weight, so this makes every weighed plate exact.
No matches. Try fewer words, or use Quick add.

Grams of protein per kg of body weight. 1.6 to 2.2 suits strength training.
Your device does not have a step counting sensor
Notify when step counting is paused
Stand straight against a wall and measure from the floor to your crotch, the same as a trouser inseam.
Your step length turns steps into distance and calories. Calibrating it is the biggest accuracy boost you can give Taro.

Go outside with open sky, away from tall buildings, and wait for the GPS signal before walking. The steps below guide you through a few paces so Taro learns how your stride changes. Each session makes it better.
Walk a distance you know exactly, like a running track lap, at your usual pace. Tap start at the beginning and stop at the end.
Keep walking. At least 3 good samples are needed.
No GPS fix yet. Go outside with a clear view of the sky and wait a minute before walking.
GPS is too weak for calibration here. Try somewhere more open, or use Known distance instead.
Not enough steps are being detected. Keep walking steadily with the phone in your hand or pocket.
Precise location is needed for GPS calibration. It is only used while this screen is open.
Turn on location to use GPS calibration.
Walk at least 50 steps for a reliable result.
Measure how accurate your steps and distance are
These tests measure the real error on your phone. Use a different walk from the one you calibrated with, or the distance test will look better than it is.
Tap start, walk at your usual pace while counting every step in your head, then tap stop and enter your count. 200 steps is a good test.
Walk a distance you know exactly, like a running track lap. Tap start at the beginning and stop at the end.
Tap any number or label to see what it means
Everything your body has burned since the day started: resting, walking, workouts and digestion. The goal is today\'s need, your projected burn for the whole day.

What your body burns just to stay alive: heart, lungs, brain, keeping warm. Worked out from your weight, height, age and sex, adjusted by what Taro has learned about you, and 5% lower while you sleep. It fills in steadily through the day.
Calories from your steps, worked out minute by minute from your pace, step length, weight and any climbing. Adjusted by your learned walking factor.
Workouts you logged, estimated from how hard the activity is and how long it lasted, on top of resting burn. Adjusted by your learned workout factor.
Breaking down food takes energy too, about 10% of everything you burn.

How much you can still eat today. Taro takes today\'s need (resting, walking and workouts so far, what you usually do for the rest of the day, and digestion), applies your goal and subtracts what you logged. The ± is how sure Taro is about your burn. It narrows as you log food and weigh in.
Cut, maintain or bulk, and how many kcal a day to move by. Tap the chip to change it, hold it to see this again.
Your target is your weight times the grams per kg you set. 1.6 g per kg suits most people who train. Tap the line to change it, hold it to see this again.
Your target is lower than what your body burns at rest. Eating this little for long can cost muscle and energy, so a smaller cut is usually better.
Mark a day when you skipped logging something. Taro then leaves that day\'s food out when it learns your burn, so a half logged day doesn\'t make it think you ate very little.
Food you logged on this day, grouped by meal. Tap + Add to log into a meal, the time chip to move a whole meal, or an entry to change it. Edit lets you add, rename, reorder or delete meals.
When you burned and ate through the day. Per hour shows each hour, Running total shows how the day added up. Shaded blocks are sleep. Tap the chart for any hour.
What an ordinary day costs you: resting burn plus your average walking and workouts over the last 14 days, plus digestion.
Where today\'s burn should end up if the rest of the day goes like your usual weekday or weekend over the last 28 days. This is today\'s need.

Taro compares what you log with how your weight moves and learns how your body differs from the formulas. It can only tell apart things that change from day to day, so steady habits like always missing cooking oil end up in the baseline. That is fine, because your target then matches the way you log.
How your total daily burn compares with the standard formulas. This is the number Taro is most sure about, and every burn figure on this tab uses it.
The part of your burn that is the same every day. It covers your metabolism and any steady logging habits, like food you always forget, because the scale cannot tell those apart.

How your walking burn compares with the formula. The scale only sees totals, so Taro can learn this only when your activity changes from week to week, like a lazy week followed by a hiking week. Until then it shows Needs more variety and the difference stays in the daily burn above.

How your logged workouts compare with their estimates. With a steady routine this can\'t be told apart from the baseline, so Taro only learns it when your training volume changes over weeks, like time off followed by a heavy block.
Your weight without the day to day water swings from salt, carbs and hard sessions. The water part fades within a few days.
Where your weight is heading if you keep eating like your last two weeks of logged days.
Dots are your weigh-ins. The line is your real weight with water swings filtered out.
How much the trend line moved over the last 7 days.
Workouts you added on this day. Log them from the + at the top. Don\'t log walks or runs, your steps already count them.
Your total burn for each day, with today so far. Days without tracking stay empty.
Weigh in to start. Taro learns how much you really burn from your weigh-ins and food logs, then every number here adjusts to you.
Learning: %1$d of %2$d logged food days, %3$d of %4$d weigh-ins. Until then the numbers stay close to the formula.
Learned from %1$d logged food days and %2$d weigh-ins. Every burn number on this tab uses it.

Resting burn uses the Mifflin-St Jeor equation and your profile, so update your weight when it changes. Active burn covers walking and running measured by steps, plus the activities you log. Every number adds about 10% for digesting food. Daily need uses your average active burn over the last 14 tracked days.
Add your age and sex so Taro can estimate your resting burn and daily calorie need.
Your changes have not been saved yet.
Nothing logged yet. Add workouts your steps don\'t capture, like the gym or cycling.
Estimated from typical intensity for your weight. Replace it with your watch\'s number if you have one.
Don\'t log walks or runs, your steps already count them. Gym machines often show total calories including resting burn, so enter the active number when you can.
However you normally walk. Fast is fine if that is how you walk.
Like strolling with a friend. This shows how your steps change when you slow down.
Faster than usual, or a light jog to calibrate running. Tap Next to skip.
Tap Stop to review and save. Walking longer only adds more samples.
Enough pace variety to learn how your stride changes
Vary your pace a little more to learn how your stride changes
Resting + steps + logged activities + digestion. Days Taro didn\'t track stay empty.
Cutting 300 to 500 kcal a day loses weight steadily. Bulking usually needs 200 to 400 kcal a day extra.
This is below your resting burn. Eating that little for long is not recommended without medical advice.
%1$s. Steps before this count toward the previous day.
Weigh yourself regularly, ideally each morning, to see your real trend and keep your calorie numbers accurate.
Weigh at the same time each day, ideally in the morning before eating. The trend smooths out daily ups and downs.
Keep logging. Pace feedback starts after about 10 days of weigh-ins.
On track: %1$s per week, right where you planned.
Slower than planned: %1$s per week against %2$s. Your real calorie need may differ from the estimate.
Faster than planned: %1$s per week against %2$s.
Losing fast: %1$s per week. Consider eating a bit more to protect muscle.
Gaining fast: %1$s per week, likely more fat than muscle. Consider eating a bit less.
Your trend is going up (%1$s per week) while you are cutting.
Your trend is going down (%1$s per week) while you are bulking.
Drifting %1$s per week. Set a calorie goal if this is intended.
Log today\'s weight to keep your trend accurate.
The line marks 7 hours. Stars show nights in the healthy range.
Averaging %1$s. Aim for 7 to 9 hours. Short sleep makes cutting harder and costs muscle.
Averaging %1$s, a little short. An extra 30 to 60 minutes would help recovery and appetite.
Averaging %1$s, right in the healthy range. Keep it up.
Averaging %1$s. That\'s on the long side. Worth checking if this is typical for you.
Your bedtime varies by about %1$d minutes. A steadier schedule helps sleep quality.
Steps, energy, weight and sleep, all on your phone.
Height and weight set your step length and calories. They stay on this phone and you can change them in Settings.
All optional. Age and sex sharpen your calorie numbers, leg length sharpens distance.
Restore a full backup, or step history from a CSV
This replaces the data on this phone with the file\'s contents. A full backup restores everything, including weight, sleep, activities and settings. Continue?
Use offline Activity Recognition API to ignore steps when you\'re in a car, bus, or on a bike. Requires Google Play Services
